get.description: It is the resolver's screen and it has no other verb — no resolve, no close, no dismiss, no acknowledge. Closing an issue is a fact of the resume command on the processing resource (registers D7, D8), so this class holds the projection and no write model at all, and a route that would close one cannot be added here without adding a command no source names. The collection is unpaginated like the orders list: one items envelope, no parameter (element 11 D-11-5).
get.summary: Element 17's one route: the open warehouse-reality gaps, served from the read model and from nothing else.

get.description: The handler holds the projection and no write model, so the read path cannot drift into the aggregate (http.no-write-model-in-read). The contract of element 11 asserts no page on this collection and element 15 says the list has no pagination, so the route takes no paging parameters and answers items alone; a page would be a bound no source names (element 11 Q-11-1).
get.summary: Element 15's one route: the employee's current orders, served from the read model and from nothing else.

post.description: The handler validates the command, calls OrderIntakeService once and maps the answer back — 201 for the delivery that opened the processing, 200 for a repeated orderHash, because idempotency is stated in the answer rather than as a second resource or a second error (element 11 D-11-2). A refused order never reaches this adapter: Order raises the refusal and the one advice answers 422 ORDER_INCOMPLETE.
post.summary: Element 12's one route: the finished order arrives from checkout and leaves as a processing.

get.description: Both the employee and the resolver scope reach it (element 11's auth matrix): a resolver deciding a resume has to see what is held, and the payload carries no customer-facing field the customer scope could not see — that scope has its own resource (element 18, D-11-4).
get.summary: The state read of element 11's processing resource: the one payload every command of the resource answers, served for whoever opens the order.

post.description: A granted claim is 201 — a claim is a fact that did not exist before, and one claim emits one event (RULE-8). A repeated claim by the same employee answers 200 with the same state (element 11 D-11-2). The refusal is not built here: the aggregate raises it and the one advice answers 409 with the guard's own reason. The request takes no body on purpose — the claimer is the assignee, so the assignee is the caller's own identity read from the token (RULE-5). The empty command record keeps the route a command and keeps the body optional.
post.summary: Element 07's one route: an employee claims one order, and leaves with the claim or with the refusal.

get.description: Nothing is rendered here. The bytes come from ParcelLabelProjection, which stores them on the first print and serves the stored document afterwards, so a reprint never registers a parcel and never consumes a number (element 06 RULE-9). A parcel that does not exist yet answers a refusal through the one advice rather than an empty document.
get.summary: The consignment note of element 06 on the wire: GET …/documents/label answers the carrier's document as application/pdf, byte for byte what the carrier printed.

get.description: The handler holds the projection and no write model, so the read path cannot drift into the aggregate (http.no-write-model-in-read). The list is generated per request — it is a snapshot, and no source says it is regenerated under a walking employee (element 10 DEFAULT-3).
get.summary: Element 10's one route: the walk an assigned employee performs, served from the query handler and from nothing else.

get.description: The route is this service's own — element 11 fixes the paths of the processing resource, the pick list and the snapshot, and names none for the workstation, whose payload is the two regions of W1 composed (recorded in docs/phase-1-decisions.md). It is a read: nothing on this screen writes, and the actions of the other views' actors — readiness, issues, resume — are not reachable from it.
get.summary: Element 16's read surface: the one screen an assigned employee works from.

get.description: It is a resource of its own and not a filtered projection of the employee's snapshot (D-11-4): the scope that reaches it is fulfillment-customer, the payload carries no assignee and no issue, and the handler holds no write model, so the read path cannot drift into the aggregate (http.no-write-model-in-read). No ownership check is made — the order carries no customer identity to compare against, and the mapping is out of scope (register D13, element 18 Q-18-2). The scope alone decides who may ask.
get.summary: Element 18's one route: the customer's view of one processing, served from the read model and from nothing else.
